newsitem.title: UK: FTSE International launches pan-European stock index.
newsitem.headline: FTSE International launches pan-European stock index.

text.p: London and Amsterdam stock market groups teamed up Thursday to promote two pan-European indices aimed at allowing investors to bet on the direction of all the continent's top equities in a single trade.
They said the alliance would create the first truly liquid market for trading pan-European stock index futures and options.

Under the terms of the deal, FTSE International -- which manages the major British stock indexes and is owned by the Financial Times and the London Stock Exchange -- will operate Amsterdam's existing Eurotop 100 index.
It will also introduce a complementary and wider-based European index called the FTSE Eurotop 300.
FTSE International said the indices would effectively replace its existing pan-European Eurotrack indices.

"They will supercede and improve upon the Eurotrack 100 and 200," said Steven Vale, FTSE International's policy and communications manager. "The new indices will use home bourse prices and will be better to use."

The Eurotrack indices were based on prices quoted in London for major continental stocks, but trading volumes through the London market have declined in recent years, making London prices a less-useful guide.
Vale said the indices anticipated a growing interest in pan-European products allied to European monetary union.

Amsterdam, which currently lists futures and options on the FTSE Eurotop 100, will also list the FTSE Eurotop 300 for options trading. Talks are underway with LIFFE, the London futures and options exchange, to trade derivatives on the two indices.

Mark Makepeace, managing director of FTSE International, said: "The integration of the European markets has begun and this process will certainly speed up as we move close to the introduction of the Euro in 1999."

"We have seen a significant increase in demand for pan-European index-linked products in the OTC (over-the-counter) market this year," Makepeace said. "These indices will meet this demand and be the basis for exchange-traded derivaties in the run-up to EMU."
FTSE International said the FTSE Eurotop 300 represented the largest 300 companies in Europe, covering 13 countries and providing exposure to around 65 percent of total market capitalisation.
It would cover companies included in existing indexes such as the FTSE 100, DAX 30 and CAC 40. Real-time foreign exchange and share price data to calculate the indexes will be supplied by Reuters.
Trading volume in the Eurotop 100 reached an average daily 31.7 million ECU in the first quarter of 1997, compared with 19.5 million through 1996.
